title: The yield strength of a body when its shape was set, by material, and how the materials mix (GEN.1158, physics/roundness.py)
note: This file is where measured strengths drop in. Every number here is a stand-in (registry rows RN1 to RN7, section 6.126 of the gap filling plan); a material gives either 'strength_pa' (a measured strength at the scale of a body, Pa) or 'round_radius_km' with 'reference_density_kg_m3' (the mean radius at which bodies of that material and density were seen to turn round; the strength that rounds a body at that size is worked out from it). 'same_as' gives a material the strength of another until it has its own. 'mixing' names a rule of physics/roundness.py (MIXING_RULES) and its numbers; 'porosity' names a rule of POROSITY_RULES. A new rule is one function and one name; the engine's interface (ice fraction, metal fraction, porosity in; strength, round radius, roundness ratio out) does not change.

ice.label: water ice and the other ices of an icy moon, warm when the shape was set
ice.source: Lineweaver and Norman 2010 (arXiv:1004.1091) Fig. 2: Mimas 198 km round, Hyperion 140 km not

rock.label: silicate rock of an asteroid or rocky moon
rock.source: Lineweaver and Norman 2010 (arXiv:1004.1091) Fig. 2: Pallas 275 km and Vesta 265 km round, Juno 115 km not

metal.label: iron and nickel metal
metal.source: planetary-material-strength-2026-10-31.md section 7: weak source, range 30 to 300 MPa

mixing.source: planetary-material-strength-2026-10-31.md section 7: ice is the matrix while solids are under 40 percent of the volume, solids carry the load over 70 percent, geometric between (Durham 1997 for hard grains in ice)

porosity.source: research proposes sigma exp(-b phi), b 4 to 7; off here because it makes Proteus (porous, ice-rich, 210 km, not round) round. 'coefficient' is used by the 'exponential' rule only

temperature.source: planetary-material-strength-2026-10-31.md section 7 (Schulson and Renshaw 2022 scaled 0.1; frozen soil exponent Wan et al. 2024)
